verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission targets launch as early as April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Launch date April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC... On March 12, after a Flight Readiness Review (FRR), seven two-hour launch windows were announced for 1–6 and April 30, with the first launch window being on April 1, 2026.
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly states the launch occurred on April 1, 2026, after targeting that date following delays and reviews, matching the claim's phrasing of 'targets as early as'.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will send four astronauts on a 10-day trip around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Crew size 4... Mission duration 9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes... Artemis II (April 1–11, 2026) was a crewed lunar flyby mission... over an approximately ten-day trip.
verifications.reasoning: R1 specifies 4 crew on a ~10-day lunar flyby (9 days +), corroborated by R2, R3, R8 describing 10-day mission with 4 astronauts around the Moon.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first crewed lunar mission in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: It was the first crewed flight... beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972... first crewed lunar flight... since Apollo 17 in 1972.
verifications.reasoning: R1 explicitly states first crewed beyond LEO since Apollo 17 (1972, >50 years), matching claim; supported by R2, R3.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will send astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Members: Reid Wiseman (commander), Victor Glover (pilot), Christina Koch (mission specialist), Jeremy Hansen (mission specialist)... crewed lunar flyby.
verifications.reasoning: R1 lists exact crew names for the lunar flyby mission; confirmed in R2, R3.

verifications.claim: The primary aim of Artemis II is to test critical life support systems on the Orion spacecraft and the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The mission's primary goal was to validate the Orion spacecraft's systems, crew operations... evaluating the performance of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket along with the Orion spacecraft... crew evaluated life support and other critical spacecraft systems.
verifications.reasoning: R1 describes primary goal as validating Orion systems including life support, and SLS performance; directly supports, though phrasing emphasizes Orion more.

verifications.claim: Artemis I (2022) successfully completed an uncrewed flight test.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: After the uncrewed Artemis I mission in November 2022... Artemis 1 successfully proved that the SLS, Orion... are capable.
verifications.reasoning: R1 and R2 confirm Artemis I as successful uncrewed test in 2022.

verifications.claim: Artemis II (2026) is a crewed lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Artemis II (April 1–11, 2026) was a crewed lunar flyby mission.
verifications.reasoning: R1 explicitly identifies Artemis II (2026) as crewed lunar flyby.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Artemis 3... will be launched by mid-2027... Artemis III is proposed for 2027.
verifications.reasoning: R5 states mid-2027 launch; R2 aligns with 2027 proposal post-changes.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is planned as a technological test.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Artemis 3... changed Artemis 3 to another demonstration mission... test essential technologies... low-Earth orbit designed to test essential technologies.
verifications.reasoning: R2 and R5 describe Artemis III as demonstration/technological test (docking, life support, etc.) instead of landing.

verifications.claim: Subsequent landings from 2028 aim for the lunar south pole.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Artemis 4 will now be the first lunar landing mission... down to the Moon's South Pole... a new Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon... near the moon’s south pole.
verifications.reasoning: R2 and R5 confirm landings starting Artemis 4 in 2028 targeting south pole.

verifications.claim: The Artemis missions rely on partnerships with commercial entities for landers.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: testing the meeting and docking procedure with one or both of the lunar landers in development. One is being made by SpaceX and one by Blue Origin.
verifications.reasoning: R2 explicitly mentions commercial partners SpaceX and Blue Origin for landers.

verifications.claim: The Artemis missions have international collaborators including the Canadian Space Agency.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen... selected by the Canadian Space Agency as part of a 2020 treaty between the United States and Canada.
verifications.reasoning: R1 details CSA participation via Hansen and treaty for Artemis.
